Bitbucket app password substitutes full account credentials for API and Git operations; scope includes repo read/write and may include admin and pipeline access.
Gitalk OAuth client_id+client_secret pair enables GitHub OAuth impersonation for comment auth; client_secret elevates from mere identifier but scope is limited to issue commenting workflows.
Classic GitHub PAT (ghp_ prefix) typically carries broad repo-write scopes plus read:org and other grants chosen at creation; no fine-grained restriction enforced by design.
GitHub OAuth access token (gho_ prefix) is user-scoped to the authorizing account's granted scopes; can include repo-write and admin:org depending on app's requested permissions.
GitHub App installation token (ghu_/ghs_ prefix) can hold org-admin or all-repos write if App was installed with broad permissions; server-to-server tokens are machine-level and hard to trace.
GitHub refresh token (ghr_ prefix) cannot directly authenticate API calls; must be exchanged for an access token requiring the client_secret as well — reduces standalone exploitability.
GitHub OAuth Client ID is a public identifier intentionally exposed in browser-visible OAuth flows; alone it grants no access and poses no direct secret exposure risk.
GitHub App client secret authenticates the App itself; combined with Client ID enables token minting, OAuth code exchange, and webhook validation — full App-level compromise.
Fine-grained GitHub PAT (github_pat_ prefix) is narrowly scoped by design to selected repos and specific permissions; lower blast radius than classic PAT but still source-control write access.
GitLab runner registration token allows registering a new CI runner to a project or group; attacker gains code execution in all future pipelines and access to CI secrets and artifacts.
GitLab Personal Access Token with api scope grants full REST API access including repo read/write, user impersonation possibilities, and group membership management.
GitLab pipeline trigger token initiates arbitrary pipeline runs on a project; enables code execution in CI environment, exfiltration of CI variables, and supply chain interference.
GitLab Routable PAT routes to a specific self-managed/Dedicated instance; carries same repo and API risks as a standard GitLab PAT.
Gitter access token authenticates to the Gitter/Matrix chat API; grants read/write to chat rooms for that user but limited to messaging — no source code or admin access.
